Why does A always pair with T?

A only pairs with T, and G with C, because their sizes fit just right between the two strands. Wrong pairs would make the helix lumpy and uneven.

Bakit laging magkapareha ang A at T?

Nagpapares lang ang A sa T, at ang G sa C, dahil tamang-tama ang laki nila para magkasya sa pagitan ng dalawang strand. Kung mali ang pares, magiging baku-bako ang helix.

Nganong kanunay magparis ang A ug T?

Ang A magpares ra sa T, ug ang G sa C, kay husto ra ang ilang gidak-on aron mohaom tunga-tunga sa duha ka strand. Kung sayop ang pares, mahimong baku-bako ang helix.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water, temperature, and oxygen as conditions supporting life, but it does not describe living things as biotic factors or name these conditions as abiotic factors in an ecosystem. It shares vocabulary but does not directly teach the competency's classification concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thanks to liquid water, gentle temperatures, and lots of oxygen, all kinds of life can thrive here!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water and oxygen, which are basic needs, but it does not identify the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It only states that life thrives due to certain conditions, without teaching the list of basic needs.

copy.en: Earth is the only known planet with a biosphere — a living layer covering its surface, oceans, and lower atmosphere. Thanks to liquid water, gentle temperatures, and lots of oxygen, all kinds of life can thrive here!
copy.tl: Ang Earth ang tanging kilalang planeta na may biosphere — isang buhay na layer na sumasaklaw sa ibabaw, karagatan, at mas mababang atmosphere nito. Dahil sa liquid water, katamtamang temperatura, at maraming oxygen, lahat ng uri ng buhay ay umuunlad dito!
copy.bis: Ang Yuta mao ra ang nahibaloan nga planeta nga adunay biosphere — usa ka buhi nga layer nga nagtabon sa nawong, kadagatan, ug ubos nga atmosphere. Tungod sa liquid water, katamtamang temperatura, ug daghang oxygen, tanang matang sa kinabuhi molambo dinhi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Flowing iron in the liquid outer core creates Earth's magnetic field!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how seismic wave data has been used to develop a model for the internal structure and composition of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the liquid outer core and iron, which are part of Earth's internal structure, but it does not describe how seismic wave data was used to develop a model of the internal structure and composition. The focus is on the magnetic field, not on seismic evidence or model development.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Flowing iron in the liquid outer core
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The card names the outer core, one layer of Earth's interior, but it does not create a scale drawing or represent relative thicknesses of the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core. It provides only a passing mention of one layer, not the required representation.

copy.en: Flowing iron in the liquid outer core creates Earth's magnetic field! This is why compasses point north and it shields us from the sun's harmful radiation.
copy.tl: Ang umaagos na bakal sa liquid outer core ang gumagawa ng magnetic field ng Earth! Kaya tumuturo sa north ang compass at nagpoprotekta ito sa atin mula sa harmful radiation ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang nagaagas nga puthaw sa liquid outer core mao ang naghimo sa magnetic field sa Earth! Mao ni ang hinungdan nganong ang kompas motudlo sa north ug nagpanalipod kini kanato gikan sa harmful radiation sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The oceanic crust under the seas is thinner, while the continental crust under land is thicker.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to name and describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about crust thickness but does not involve gathering information from secondary sources, nor does it name or describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth. It only mentions oceanic and continental crust without describing layers.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The oceanic crust under the seas is thinner, while the continental crust under land is thicker.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify how oceanic crust and continental crust is associated with the Earth's lithospheric plates
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oceanic and continental crust but does not identify how they are associated with Earth's lithospheric plates. It only compares their thickness, which is background information rather than direct support for the association with lithospheric plates.

copy.en: Earth's crust isn't the same thickness everywhere! The oceanic crust under the seas is thinner, while the continental crust under land is thicker.
copy.tl: Hindi pare-pareho ang kapal ng crust! Mas manipis ang oceanic crust sa ilalim ng karagatan, at mas makapal ang continental crust sa ilalim ng lupain.
copy.bis: Ang crust dili pareho ang kabaga! Mas nipis ang oceanic crust sa ilalom sa kadagatan, ug mas baga ang continental crust sa ilalom sa yuta.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about relative thickness (crust is thinnest) but does not involve creating a scale drawing or representing the relative thicknesses of the multiple layers named in the competency (crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, inner core). It provides no instructional support for the drawing skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the crust is the thinnest layer of Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how seismic wave data has been used to develop a model for the internal structure and composition of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a layer of Earth's interior but says nothing about seismic wave data or how such data was used to develop a model of internal structure and composition. The fact about crust thickness is only tangentially related to the competency's focus.

copy.en: Did you know the crust is the thinnest layer of Earth? It's super thin compared to the giant mantle and core!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na ang crust ang pinakamanipis na layer ng Mundo? Super manipis ito kumpara sa malalaking mantle at core!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang crust mao ang pinakanipis nga layer sa Kalibutan? Super nipis kini kumpara sa dako nga mantle ug core!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how seismic wave data has been used to develop a model for the internal structure and composition of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a general temperature gradient inside Earth but does not mention seismic wave data, model development, or internal composition, which are the core of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: near the core it becomes extremely hot

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions crust and core but does not create a scale drawing or represent relative thicknesses of the specified layers (lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, etc.).

copy.en: The deeper you go inside Earth, the hotter it gets! The outer crust is cool, but near the core it becomes extremely hot — that's why erupting lava is so hot!
copy.tl: Habang papalalim sa loob ng Earth, lalong umiinit! Malamig ang outer crust, pero malapit sa core ay sobrang init — kaya mainit ang lava na sumasabog!
copy.bis: Samtang molawom sa sulod sa Earth, mas moinit! Ang outer crust bugnaw, apan duol sa core init kaayo — mao nga init kaayo ang lava nga mosabog!
